chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, and Ahmad also reported it from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Kufi, who said:

One of our companions married a young girl who had not yet menstruated. When he deflowered her, blood flowed and continued flowing without stopping for about ten days. He showed her to the midwives and those women he thought had insight, but they differed; some said this is menstrual blood, others said it is virginity blood. He asked their jurists, such as Abu Hanifa and others, who said: 'This is a matter of confusion, and prayer is an obligatory duty, so let her perform ablution and pray, and let her husband abstain from her until she sees the whiteness (cessation of blood). If it is menstrual blood, prayer will not harm her, and if it is virginity blood, she has fulfilled the obligation.'

The girl did as they said, and I performed Hajj that year. When we were in Mina, I sent a message to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying: 'May I be your ransom, we have a question that has become burdensome to us. If you permit me, I will come to you and ask you about it.' He sent back: 'When the crowd subsides and the road is clear, come, God willing.'

Khalaf said: I stayed through the night until I saw the people's movement in Mina had decreased, then I headed to his tent. When I was near, I saw a black man sitting on the road. He asked, 'Who is the man?' I said, 'A man from the pilgrims.' He asked, 'What is your name?' I said, 'Khalaf ibn Hammad.' He said, 'Enter without needing permission, for he ordered me to sit here, and when you come, I will grant you entry.'

I entered, greeted, and he returned the greeting while sitting alone on his carpet, with no one else in the tent. When I stood before him, he asked me and I asked him about his state. I said to him: 'A man from your mawali married a young girl who had not yet menstruated. When he deflowered her, blood flowed and continued without stopping for about ten days. The midwives differed regarding this; some said it is menstrual blood, others said it is virginity blood. What is befitting for her to do?'

He said: 'Let her fear God. If it is menstrual blood, let her abstain from prayer until she sees purity, and let her husband abstain from her. And if it is virginity blood, let her fear God, perform ablution, pray, and her husband may come to her if he wishes.'

I said to him: 'How can they know what it is so they can do what is befitting?' He looked right and left in the tent, fearing someone might hear his speech, then he turned to me and said: 'O Khalaf, a secret of God, a secret of God! Do not broadcast it, nor teach this creation the principles of God's religion. Rather, be pleased for them with what God is pleased for them of straying.'

He said: Then he formed the number ninety with his left hand, then said: 'She should insert the cotton, then leave it for a while, then extract it gently. If the blood is encircled in the cotton, it is from virginity, and if it is splashed/pooled in the cotton, it is from menstruation.'

Khalaf said: Joy overcame me and I cried. When my crying subsided, he asked: 'What made you cry?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, who is better at this than you?' He raised his hand to the sky and said: 'By God, I do not inform you except from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), from Gabriel, from God, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: How to distinguish between menstrual blood and virginity blood in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between *hayd* (menstruation) and *istihadha* (non-menstrual bleeding) through practical diagnostic signs, specifically the 'cotton test' (*istikhdam al-qutn*) to determine if blood is pooled or flowing. Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) reveals this ruling as a divine secret transmitted from the Prophet via Gabriel, emphasizing the precision required in fiqh to ensure the validity of prayer and marital relations during periods of ambiguous bleeding.
